resources.string: Ask for an app PIN (and optionally your fingerprint) when opening WakeCtrl. Keeping the screen on carries on while it\'s locked.
WakeCtrl works fully offline: it has no internet permission, analytics or tracking. Your settings and activity log stay on this phone.
The PIN can\'t be recovered. WakeCtrl will reset its settings and automations, clear the activity log and turn the app lock off. If your phone has a screen lock, you\'ll confirm with it first.
The screen turns off as usual. Tap to keep it on.
Stopped at low battery. Automations resume once the phone charges.
Applies when you turn it on yourself (here, the tile or shortcut). Automations keep the screen on for as long as they match.
A whole number of minutes, 1 to %1$d
Each tap moves to the next length; after the last one the tile turns it off
Without \"Tap to cycle\", a tap turns it on with the timer above and the next tap turns it off. The tile shows the length while it runs.
The first tap starts the shortest. Each length starts counting again from the moment you tap. Keep at least one.
Stopped: the battery is hot (%1$s). Automations resume once it has cooled down.
Paused: the proximity sensor is covered (in a pocket or face down). It carries on when it\'s uncovered.
Tap to set battery use to Unrestricted, so Android doesn\'t stop WakeCtrl in the background.
WakeCtrl checks which app is on screen with Android\'s Usage access. It only reads the app name, on this phone, and only while the screen is on.
No limit: the screen stays on for as long as the app is open
Stays on for %1$s each time the app comes on screen
Keeps the screen on for this app only when the phone is also charging
Switch on the apps that keep the screen on. For each one you can choose \"Only while charging\", for example for a navigation app that you only want on in the car.
Handy on a dock, a car mount or a nightstand.
While a chosen Bluetooth device is connected
For example your car or a speaker. Needs the Nearby devices permission; WakeCtrl only looks at devices you\'ve already paired.
Devices you pair in Android\'s Bluetooth settings show up here.
Keep the screen on in the time windows below

A window that ends at or before its start time runs past midnight and ends the next day; the days are the days it starts. Times follow your phone\'s clock, also after a time zone or daylight-saving change.
So set hours start and end on the minute. Without it, Android may run them a few minutes late.
Pick the days the window starts on. An end at or before the start means the next day.
The screen won\'t be kept on during these hours any more.
Music, a podcast or a video playing in any app, for example lyrics or a recipe video. WakeCtrl only asks Android whether something is playing, not what.
Only for docks that tell Android the phone is docked (desk and car docks). An ordinary charger or a magnetic car mount doesn\'t: use ChargeWake for those.
Wired, USB-C or Bluetooth headphones and headsets. To pick specific Bluetooth devices, use BTWake instead.
Needed to see which app is on screen. Find WakeCtrl in the list and switch it on.
Optional: shows when WakeCtrl holds the screen, with a quick on/off button
The brightness is restored when WakeCtrl lets go. \"Allow dimming\" lets the screen dim while it stays on.
The screen dims after a while but doesn\'t turn off
Let the screen sleep while the proximity sensor is covered for a few seconds (in a pocket or face down)
This phone has no proximity sensor, so this does nothing here
Stop when the battery is hot
Turn off when the screen goes off
Switching the screen off ends keeping it awake by hand (tile or app). Automations keep working.
Notify after 3 hours of keeping the screen on while on battery
If you had it on when the phone restarted, turn it back on
Some phones (including OPPO and OnePlus) stop apps in the background. These two settings keep WakeCtrl working.
Allow other apps to control WakeCtrl

Send a broadcast to com.vknxworks.wakectrl with action com.vknxworks.wakectrl.action.ON, OFF or TOGGLE. Add a whole-number extra \"minutes\" (0 to 1440; 0 means no limit) to ON or TOGGLE to keep the screen on for that long instead of the timer. While this is off, those requests are ignored and noted in the activity log.

A file with your settings and automations (timer, screen, battery, chosen apps, Bluetooth devices and time windows), to move them to another phone or keep a copy. The app lock, the privacy settings and \"Allow other apps\" aren\'t in it and an import never changes them.
Save them to a file you choose
Replace them with the ones in a WakeCtrl settings file
Couldn\'t write the file. Nothing was exported.
Couldn\'t read the file. Nothing was changed.
That isn\'t a WakeCtrl settings file. Nothing was changed.
That file comes from a newer WakeCtrl. Update WakeCtrl first. Nothing was changed.

Your timer, screen and battery settings and all your automations will be replaced by the ones in this file (exported %1$s). After the import you'll have:

%2$s

The app lock, the privacy settings and "Allow other apps" stay as they are.
What WakeCtrl did and why, kept on this phone
Each time WakeCtrl keeps the screen on or lets go, it\'s noted here.
The saved activity log is encrypted and can\'t be opened on this phone right now. It is kept as it is and nothing is added to it. New lines are shown here but aren\'t saved until this is solved.
Shows while WakeCtrl keeps the screen on or watches for automations
Low battery, hot battery and long-session reminders
The screen turns off as usual until an automation matches
Stopped at low battery until the phone charges
Stopped because the battery is hot, until it cools down
Paused while the proximity sensor is covered
The battery reached %1$s, so the screen can turn off again. Automations resume once it has cooled down.
The battery fell to %1$d%%, so the screen can turn off again. Automations resume once the phone charges.
The screen has been on for 3 hours
WakeCtrl has kept the screen on for over 3 hours on battery. Turn it off when you don\'t need it.
Stopped at a battery temperature of %1$s
Another app sent a \"minutes\" value that isn\'t a whole number from 0 to 1440; used the timer instead
Ignored a request from another app (\"Allow other apps\" is off)
Android didn\'t let WakeCtrl start from here. Open WakeCtrl once, then try again.
Turn keep screen on on or off
carried on after Android restarted WakeCtrl
Android didn\'t let WakeCtrl start in the background, so a request was dropped. Set WakeCtrl\'s battery use to Unrestricted.
Android didn\'t let WakeCtrl start in the background, so the screen isn\'t being kept on. Set WakeCtrl\'s battery use to Unrestricted so this doesn\'t happen again.
Use your phone\'s screen lock to confirm it\'s you
Couldn\'t show the screen lock prompt
